title: CPU functional tests on ARM64 interrupted - suite count mismatch in parallel runner
signature: number of suites in expected suite|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: CPU functional tests / CPU functional tests
failed_jobs.symptom: 1 test interrupted; suite count mismatch (15 vs 60 expected) in log_2.log

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_linux_arm64
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check failed due to dependent CPU functional test job failing

key_errors: ERROR:test_parallel_runner:Number of suites in /__w/openvino/openvino/install/tests/temp/log_2.log: 15. Expected is 60 suite
root_cause: The CPU functional test parallel runner detected that log_2.log (a shard/worker log file) contained only 15 test suites instead of the expected 60. This caused the runner to report 1 interrupted test and exit with code 255. This is a known flakiness pattern in the parallel test runner on ARM64 where a worker process terminates early or a suite partition is incomplete. The PR under test changes only GPU/OCL kernel code (paged_attention_opt.cl, sdpa/paged_attention_opt.cpp, paged_attention_gpu_test.cpp) and has no coupling to ARM64 CPU functional tests, strongly suggesting this is an infrastructure/runner issue rather than a PR-induced regression.
reproduction_steps: N/A - infrastructure-level flakiness in the parallel test runner; unlikely to reproduce on local ARM64 hardware under normal conditions.
recommended_actions: Re-add the PR to the merge queue; this failure appears unrelated to the GPU-only code change.
Monitor for recurrence of 'Number of suites in log_2.log: N. Expected is 60 suite' failures on ARM64.
If recurring: investigate the parallel runner worker process (run_parallel.py) for premature exit/OOM conditions on the ARM64 runner.
prevention_strategies: Consider adding a retry mechanism in the parallel test runner for suite count mismatches. Monitor ARM64 runner resource utilization during CPU functional test runs.
historical_context: No prior occurrence of this exact suite count mismatch pattern has been recorded in the CI Doctor MQ database.
